definition: Connecting a model's output to real, verifiable sources or data instead of letting it answer from memory alone.
details: Grounded systems retrieve documents or query tools, then constrain the answer to what those sources support — which reduces hallucination and makes claims auditable. Retrieval-augmented generation is the most common way to implement it.
story: Picture a student writing an essay with the textbook open, checking every claim against a page number before they write it down. That is Grounding: connecting a model's output to real, verifiable sources or data instead of letting it answer from memory alone. And here is the clever part: grounded systems retrieve documents or query tools, then constrain the answer to what those sources support — which reduces hallucination and makes claims auditable. It turns 'I think I remember' into 'here is the receipt.' And that discipline of answering from evidence, not vibes, is Grounding.

citation.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
